It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}, and its former shrine rank was that of a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}. It was regarded as the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=guardian shrine}} of Kumagaya-go{{sfn|Coloring the History of Kumagaya|2011|p=139}}. It is also known for having “Japan’s longest {{ill|O-mikuji|ar|او ميكوجي|ca|Omikuji|cs|Omikudži|da|Omikuji|de|Omikuji|el|Ομίκουζι|es|Omikuji|et|Omikuji|fr|Omikuji|id|Omikuji|it|Omikuji|ja|おみくじ|ko|오미쿠지|ms|Omikuji|my|အိုမိခုဂျိ|pl|O-mikuji|pt|Omikuji|ru|Омикудзи|th|โอมิกูจิ|tr|Omikuji|vi|O-mikuji|zh|御神籤|qid=Q1069592}}.” {{nihongo|'''Takagi Shrine'''|高城神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. == Enshrined deity ==
* {{ill|Takamimusubi|de|Takamimusubi|es|Takami-musubi-no-kami|fa|تاکامیموسوبی|fr|Takamimusubi|id|Takamimusubi|it|Takamimusubi|ja|タカミムスヒ|ko|다카미무스비|ks|تاکامِمُسُبی|pl|Takamimusubi|ru|Такамимусуби-но ками|zh|高皇產靈尊|qid=Q125400|lt=Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto}}
** Takamimusubi-no-Mikoto is also known by the alternate name Takagi-no-Kami, and as a deity who personifies generative power, is regarded as a god who creates all things. He is revered as a deity of “matchmaking” and “safe childbirth”{{sfn|Shrines of Saitama|1992|pp=66–71}}.

== History ==
An ancient shrine recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} as “One shrine in Ōsato District: Takagi Shrine.” The shrine precincts and surrounding area lie within the {{ill|Alluvial fan|an|Cono de dechección|ar|مروحة طميية|ast|Abanicu aluvial|bg|Наносен конус|bn|পলল শাখা|ca|Con de dejecció|cs|Náplavový kužel|de|Schwemmkegel|es|Abanico aluvial|et|Uhtekuhik|eu|Alubioi-kono|fa|مخروط افکنه|fi|Alluviaalikeila|fr|Cône de déjection|gl|Abano aluvial|he|מניפת סחף|hi|जलोढ़ पंख|hu|Hordalékkúp|id|Kipas aluvial|is|Aurkeila|it|Conoide di deiezione|ja|扇状地|ka|გამოზიდვის კონუსი|kk|Ысырынды конусы|ko|선상지|la|Conus deiectionis|mn|Аллювийн сүүж|nl|Puinwaaier|no|Sedimentvifte|oc|Còne de dejeccion|pl|Stożek napływowy|pt|Leque aluvial|ro|Con de dejecție|ru|Конус выноса|sh|Aluvijalna lepeza|simple|Alluvial fan|sl|Aluvialni stožec|sr|Aluvijalna lepeza|sv|Svämkägla|ta|வண்டல் விசிறி|th|ตะกอนน้ำพารูปพัด|tr|Alüvyon yelpazesi|uk|Конус виносу|zh|沖積扇|zh_yue|沖積扇|qid=Q465088}} of the {{ill|Arakawa River (Kantō)|arz|نهر اراكاوا|ceb|Ara-kawa (suba sa Hapon, lat 35,76, long 139,76)|de|Arakawa (Bucht von Tokio)|eo|Arakaŭa (rivero)|es|Río Arakawa|eu|Arakawa ibaia|fa|آراکاوا (رود)|fr|Ara-kawa|gn|Ysyry Arakagua|id|Sungai Arakawa (Kantō)|it|Arakawa (fiume)|ja|荒川 (関東)|ko|아라카와강 (간토 지방)|my|အရခဝမြစ် (ခန်းတိုး)|nl|Arakawa (rivier)|no|Arakawa (Kantō)|pt|Rio Arakawa|ru|Аракава (река)|simple|Arakawa River|sv|Arakawa (flod)|th|แม่น้ำอารากาวะ|tr|Arakawa Nehri|uk|Річка Ара (Канто)|vi|Sông Ara|zh|荒川 (關東)|zh_yue|荒川|qid=Q625465|lt=Arakawa}}. == Womb-passing ritual ==
* Every year on June 30, a ritual called “womb-passing” ({{ill|Ōharae-shiki|fa|اوهارائه‌شیکی|fr|Ōharae-shiki|ja|大祓|ko|오하라에|simple|Ōharae-shiki|th|โอฮาราเอะ|qid=Q11261910}}) is held. It is said that by passing through a chinowa (a ring of thatch) with a diameter of four meters attached to the first torii gate on the approach, one purifies the body and is protected from misfortune{{sfn|Coloring the History of Kumagaya|2011|p=139}}.

== Annual events and festivals ==
* January 1 – New Year’s shrine visit: Charms attached to small branches are bestowed, and many people visit from midnight through early morning.
* January 15 – Coming-of-Age Ceremony
* February 3 – Setsubun Festival
* February 11 – National Foundation Festival
* April 10 – Spring Mid-Festival
* June 30 – {{ill|Ōharae-shiki|fa|اوهارائه‌شیکی|fr|Ōharae-shiki|ja|大祓|ko|오하라에|simple|Ōharae-shiki|th|โอฮาราเอะ|qid=Q11261910}}: see the womb-passing ritual section
* October 2 – Annual festival
* November 15 – {{ill|Shichi-Go-San|ar|شيشي قو سان|ca|Shichi-Go-San|da|Shichi-go-san|de|Shichi-go-san|es|Shichi-Go-San|fa|شیچی-گو-سان|fi|Shichi-go-san|fr|Shichi-go-san|hu|Sicsi-Go-Szan|hy|Սիչի-Գո-Սան|id|Shichi-Go-San|it|Shichi-Go-San|ja|七五三|ko|시치고산|lt|Šičigosan|mn|Шичигосан|ms|Shichi-Go-San|my|ရှိချိဂေါ့ဆန်း|nl|Shichi-Go-San|pl|Shichi-go-san|pt|Shichi-Go-San|ru|Сити-го-сан|simple|Shichi-Go-San|sv|Shichi-go-san|tr|Shichi-Go-San|vi|Shichi-Go-San|zh|七五三|qid=Q1072387}}

يىلى|uk|1906|ur|1906ء|uz|1906|vec|1906|vi|1906|vls|1906|vo|1906|wa|1906|war|1906|wuu|1906年|xmf|1906|yi|1906|za|1906 nienz|zea|1906|zh|1906年|zh_classical|一九〇六年|zh_min_nan|1906 nî|zh_yue|1906年|qid=Q2049}} (Meiji 39)<ref name="kumakei20171208">{{Cite web|Japanese|url=https://kumagaya.keizai.biz/headline/237/|title=“Yōkamachi” Tori-no-Ichi at Takagi Shrine in Kumagaya|work=Kumagaya Keizai Shimbun|publisher=Webuya Co., Ltd.|date=2017-12-08|accessdate=2018-11-26}}</ref> and is generally also called Yōkamachi (the Eighth-Day Market)<ref name="kumakei20171208"/>. A market is held on the Day of the Rooster, where people purchase various items to welcome the New Year. Over time, many visitors began seeking lucky rakes and household altars, and stalls selling various goods and sweets are set up, creating a lively atmosphere. In Saitama Prefecture, Tori-no-Ichi events begin in Chichibu on December 2, followed by Kawagoe (3rd), Fukaya (5th), Gyōda (6th), and Kumagaya (8th), each with fixed dates. In the case of Takagi Shrine, it is not held on the Day of the Rooster but on the 8th, hence the name Yōkamachi<ref name="kumakei20171208"/>.
